picks.title: Tamber 2.0 splits its assistive AI into five apps, adds Windows, gestures and natural-language DAW commands
picks.excerpt: Tamber 2.0 restructures the assistive (non-generative) platform into five connected creative apps and adds native Windows support, gesture control and natural-language DAW commands. It is pitched as a system that helps you drive your existing tools and find sounds, not a prompt box that spits out finished songs.
picks.rationale: The clearest non-generative model of AI in a studio: it drives the DAW and library you already own, and it now runs on Windows too.

picks.title: Apple Music will show 'Made With AI' labels — but only if labels and distributors self-declare
picks.excerpt: Apple Music told industry partners on Aug 20 that it will show visible 'Made With AI' labels later this year for tracks whose songs, lyrics, artwork or music videos were materially generated with AI. Unlike Spotify and Deezer, Apple runs no detection of its own — labels and distributors have to self-declare via the AI Transparency Tags it quietly introduced in March.
picks.rationale: Anyone shipping music this year now has a disclosure step at delivery: Apple does not detect, so the tag is on you and your distributor.

picks.title: SSG Audio's Loudness Pro recalculates its clip/limit split thousands of times a second
picks.excerpt: SSG Audio's Loudness Pro is a one-knob mastering limiter whose AI engine recalculates the clip/limit split thousands of times per second instead of holding a fixed threshold, aiming to hit a loudness target without pumping or flattened transients. It adds automatic dither for 16-bit exports and runs at roughly 5ms latency.
picks.rationale: A concrete change to the last stage of every mix: a moving clip/limit split instead of a fixed threshold, at 5ms latency you can leave inserted.

picks.title: VAEMI's Synterra turns plants, fungi, light and touch into generative parts you can key-lock
picks.excerpt: VAEMI's Synterra is a standalone 'bio-interactive' generative synth that reads changing data from plants, fungi, fruit, conductive surfaces, light and touch and turns it into evolving notes and rhythms via a probability engine. A MIDI Scale Mode lets an external keyboard or DAW constrain its generative output to your harmony.
picks.rationale: Generative music sourced from physical sensors rather than a prompt, and MIDI Scale Mode keeps the output inside the key of the track you are writing.

picks.title: Vibe coding has come for music plugins — the bottleneck is now taste, not DSP
picks.excerpt: AI-assisted coding has made building your own plugin cheap enough that solo producers and established audio companies alike are shipping bespoke tools. Developers interviewed say the bottleneck has moved from writing DSP code to knowing what to ask for — human direction and taste still decide whether the result is usable.
picks.rationale: Working developers describing what actually ships: building a bespoke plugin is now a taste problem, which puts one-off tools inside a producer's reach.
